one_month_reasoning: The window to 2026-11-08 very likely contains Q3 2026 results. The date was not yet announced when I searched; prior years reported on Oct 29, 2025 and Oct 31, 2024, so expect about Oct 28-29. This is the main event. Q3 EPS consensus is $2.43, with 14 downward vs 3 upward revisions in the last 30 days (Alpha Vantage), so the bar has been lowered. Management guided Q3 net sales growth in the high teens and stronger Q4, but that assumes baseline power outages. Q2 outages were more than 30% below baseline, and the 2026 hurricane season had no hurricanes as of Sept 2 (strong El Nino). So residential home-standby and portable sales are the downside risk, while data-center shipments ($450M FY26 guide) and any update on the second hyperscaler deal or Amazon 2027 volumes are the upside. The Q4 guide and 2027 framing will likely move the stock more than the Q3 print. The stock has already rallied from $187 (week of Sept 7) to $225 on the Amazon deal and Oct 5-8 analyst actions (KeyBanc upgrade, Piper initiation at Buy, Cantor target cut to $297). With an earnings event in the window I use roughly the stock's normal monthly volatility (56%/3.5 = 16%; I use 16.5%), centred at about $223.5, a slight negative tilt from the residential/weather risk. I do not take a strong directional view.

fair_value.method: 80% P/E: Oct-2027 NTM EPS of $12.54 (skeptic FY27 $11.50, about 11% below the $12.97 consensus, rolled 3 quarters into FY28 at +12%) x 18.4x, a segment-mix multiple inside the peer range, gives $231. 20% DCF (WACC 12.4%, FCF margin rising from 8% to 10.5%) gives $124 a year out. Blend is about $209.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 $12.54 = 0.25 x FY27 $11.50 + 0.75 x FY28 $12.88; x 18.4x (segment-mix multiple: 50% residential peers 14.5x + 50% C&I at avg of CMI 15.9x and data-center electrical median 28.6x)

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $12.97 implies +34% on FY26 $9.69. FY26 includes ~$0.90 of non-recurring tariff refunds, so underlying FY26 is ~$8.79 and consensus implies ~+48%. I haircut by ~11% for four reasons. (1) Management says hyperscale margins are lower than non-hyperscale and it gets no above-market price premium. (2) The Amazon warrant (up to 1.69M shares) acts as consideration to a customer, and its $2.4B 2027-28 volumes are 'expected', not minimums. (3) Residential guidance assumes baseline outages that are not occurring. (4) FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin ex-tariff is only 18.5-19.5%. $11.50 sits just above the Alpha Vantage consensus low of $11.28.

Amazon's expected deliveries of $2.4B span 2027 and 2028, so DC revenue plateaus rather than compounding. Capacity is to triple from the $1.25B year-end-2026 run-rate over 12 months, which supports growth but with lower hyperscale margins. I assume growth slows from ~31% consensus FY27 to ~12%.

Q2 2026 sales split Residential $621M vs C&I $557M (~50/50). Residential is valued at the median of AOS 14.47, LII 14.43 and CARR 18.19 = 14.47x. C&I is valued at the average of the closest genset competitor CMI (15.94x) and the median of the 8 data-center/electrical peers (VRT 30.75, AAON 31.19, POWL 29.74, NVT 28.67, ETN 28.47, CAT 27.78, MOD 25.96, HUBB 21.78 -> 28.57x) = 22.26x. Blend 0.5 x 14.47 + 0.5 x 22.26 = 18.37x.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCF 2027-30 $488M/$604M/$725M/$807M (revenue $6.10B growing 10/8/6%, FCF margin 8/9/10/10.5%); terminal growth 3.5%; WACC 12.4% (CoE 13.3% = 5.24% + 1.92 x 4.20%; after-tax debt ~3.8%; D/(D+E) 9.1%); net debt $1.064B; 60.0M diluted shares; value $112 today, rolled forward 0.8yr at CoE to $124

inputs_detail.derivation: ~5% below the $6.40B consensus. Allows for slippage in the DC ramp (capacity triples within 12 months, with 30% outsourced packaging) and Amazon volumes that are expected, not minimum.
2026 FCF/sales = 350/4,930 = 7.1%, depressed by capex at ~4.5% of sales that management expects to stay below 5%. I assume gradual improvement as capex normalises.
Amazon expected deliveries of $2.4B over 2027-28; decelerating after the DC step-up.
Q2 2026 interest expense $16.8M x 4 / total debt $1,329M = 5.05%; ~25% tax rate is a judgment (21% federal + state).
Short-term $48.3M + current LTD $32.1M + LTD $1,249.0M - cash $264.9M at 2026-06-30
Q2 2026 diluted weighted average 59.64M + 0.31M immediately vested Amazon warrant shares ~= 59.95M
Below the nominal risk-free rate of 5.24%. A mature industrial growth rate.

bear.story: Weather and execution: a second straight sub-baseline outage year (El Nino) drives residential down. Hyperscale volumes come at lower margins and the Amazon 'expected' deliveries slip, so FY27 EPS is about $9.75 (flat ex-tariff refunds). With data-center growth no longer credible, the stock is valued like residential durables (~14.5x): ~$140. That is roughly where it traded in early January 2026.

base.story: Data-center deliveries ramp roughly as contracted, but at lower hyperscale margins with no price premium. Residential is muted, so FY27 EPS is about $11.5-12, below the $12.97 consensus. On NTM EPS of ~$12.3 x ~18x the stock ends roughly flat.

bull.story: The second hyperscaler contract is finalised, an active 2027 storm season revives home standby, capacity tripling lands on time, and FY27 EPS beats consensus. NTM EPS of ~$14.5 x ~21.5x (today's forward multiple) gives about $310, near the 52-week high of $296.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 14.4x (LII) to 31.2x (AAON); EV/EBITDA (TTM, as reported by StockAnalysis; forward EV/EBITDA was not available on a free verifiable source) 10.4x (AOS) to 35.0x (VRT). There are two clusters: residential durables at 14-18x P/E, and data-center electrical/thermal at 26-31x, with CMI (15.9x) as the direct genset competitor in between.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 18.4x NTM P/E: inside the range, about 8.5 turns below the 12-peer median of 26.9x. Today GNRC trades at 21.7x forward (StockAnalysis) and ~17.3x FY27 consensus ($224.94/$12.97).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount to the median is a mix effect, not an asserted haircut. (1) About half of sales are residential (Q2: $621M of $1,173M), which belongs with dealer-channel residential durables (AOS/LII/CARR median 14.5x). That segment's demand depends on outage frequency: Q2 outages were more than 30% below baseline and there were no hurricanes as of Sept 2, 2026. (2) In C&I, GNRC's data-center product is a genset like CMI's (15.9x), not a proprietary power/thermal system like VRT/NVT. Management states hyperscale margins are lower and it gets no above-market price premium. Data-center revenue rests on two hyperscalers, and the Amazon volumes are 'expected' with a warrant attached. So C&I gets the average of CMI and the DC-electrical median, not the DC-electrical multiple. (3) GNRC's 5Y beta of 1.92 and its 2021-23 boom-bust history argue against a premium. These features are structural (segment mix, customer concentration, product type) and will persist through the 12-month horizon.

thesis_break_reason: At $160 the stock would be pricing NTM EPS of ~$12.5 at under 13x, below every peer including the residential durables. Alternatively it would be pricing EPS falling toward the high-$9s. Either signals something fundamental: Amazon or other hyperscale deliveries slipping or being renegotiated (volumes are 'expected', not minimums), data-center margins compressing, or a structural break in home-standby demand, rather than ordinary 56%-vol noise. It is also well below the ~$175-187 level where the stock sat just before the Amazon deal (Sept 2026), so the market would effectively be assigning that contract zero value.

key_uncertainties: Whether Amazon's $2.4B 2027-28 'expected' deliveries convert in full and on time. The 8-K does not describe them as minimum commitments, and termination terms are redacted.
Hyperscale gross margins: management concedes they are lower than non-hyperscale and that Generac earns no price premium versus Caterpillar/Cummins/Kohler.
Outage frequency: residential guidance assumes baseline outages, but Q2 2026 ran more than 30% below baseline and El Nino suppressed the hurricane season.
Quality of FY26 earnings: ~$0.90 of FY26 EPS came from tariff refunds that management expects to be offset by higher tariffs.
Capacity tripling within 12 months, with ~30% third-party packaging: execution risk mirrors the 2022 over-expansion that Spruce Point flagged.
High rates (10-yr UST 5.24%) and a 5Y beta of 1.92 make the multiple sensitive to macro shocks.
Litigation tail: securities-suit appeal and PHS arbitration (June 2027). Neither looks material to valuation on current evidence.
reasoning: Lane: skeptic. I looked for what would make the consensus ($287.78 avg target, 16 of 22 Buy/Strong Buy, FY27 EPS $12.97) wrong on the downside, then weighed it. The bear evidence is mostly from primary sources. (a) Earnings quality: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin of 24.8% includes a $71M tariff refund (~6pts, ~$0.90 EPS), and the FY26 guide was raised only by the refund (ex-tariff still 18.5-19.5%). Underlying FY26 EPS is ~$8.8, so consensus FY27 implies roughly +48% growth. (b) Data-center economics: on the Q2 call management said hyperscale margin profiles are lower and that Generac is not getting an above-market price premium. The Amazon 8-K pairs the $2.4B 2027-28 'expected' deliveries with a warrant for up to 1.69M shares (~2.9%) struck at $200.93, vesting with up to $8B of purchases. That amounts to a price concession, and no minimum purchase obligation is disclosed. (c) Residential: outages ran more than 30% below baseline in Q2, guidance assumes a return to baseline, and the 2026 season had no hurricanes as of Sept 2 under a strong El Nino. Q3 EPS estimates saw 14 downward revisions in 30 days. (d) Insiders: no buys and $3.66M of sales in 3 months, all under 10b5-1 plans and small in size, so this is a weak signal. What I did not find also matters. There is no current short report (the only one, Spruce Point 2022, targeted capacity expansion into a peak, which is a useful analogue for today's capacity tripling). Credit is calm: term loans carry fair values at or above carrying value (TLA $693M vs $697M; TLB $493M vs $489M), net debt is ~$1.06B, and Debt/EBITDA is 2.15x. Litigation looks contained (securities suit dismissed and on appeal; PHS arbitration not until June 2027). Short interest is modest at 4.3% of float. So the skeptic case is about growth and margin rather than balance sheet or accounting. Valuation: a segment-mix P/E (18.4x on Oct-27 NTM EPS of $12.54, haircut ~11% from consensus) gives $231. A DCF at a 12.4% WACC (high rates, beta 1.92) gives only $124, which shows how much of the price rests on near-term EPS multiples rather than cash flow. FY26 FCF of ~$350M means a ~2.6% FCF yield on the $13.3B market cap. The blended fair value is ~$209, about 7% below spot. Distribution: I averaged a three-scenario lognormal mixture (bear $150 / base $222 / bull $310 at 25/50/25, each with 25-30% dispersion) with a single lognormal (median $215, sigma 0.50, a little below the 56% realized vol, which was inflated by deal-announcement jumps). This puts the median near $219, P(>=225) at 47% and the left tail fat (P(<157) about 22%). The upside tail is trimmed relative to pure lognormal because the bull case needs consensus to be beaten while EPS is already re-based. Research limits: Twelve Data statistics, estimates and insider endpoints, and Alpha Vantage overview, are behind paywalls and were not worked around. sec.gov refused a generic scripted user agent for documents, so filings were read via WebFetch. Some MarketBeat, Nasdaq and Seeking Alpha pages returned 403/503, and no current Moody's/S&P rating could be found. Of 31 sources, 11 are in-lane: the 12 peer pages and the rate/ERP inputs required by the comps and DCF rules dilute the ratio. Excluding those, 11 of 17 (65%) are in-lane. At least 3 (Amazon warrant 8-K terms, term-loan fair values in the 10-Q, Form 4/144 insider data, and the 2022 Spruce Point short thesis) are unlikely to be found by other lanes.
